tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary:
PAY-4411 is fixed: amounts now render with their currency's own number of decimals (CLP/JPY none, USD/EUR/BRL/MXN/COP two, KWD three). `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race ./...` are clean.

**Cause:** `money.Amount.Decimal()` hardcoded two decimals (`m/100`, `%02d`) for every currency. Parsing and storage were already correct, so 15000 CLP was stored as 15000 and only displayed as "150.00". The fee calculation was also correct; it only looked wrong because it went through the same formatter (435 CLP shown as "4.35").

**Fix (`money/amount.go`):** `Decimal()` now uses the currency's exponent. Negative amounts keep the minus sign, including values under one major unit ("-0.005" KWD). USD output is unchanged.

Because every response field and the webhook payloads go through `Decimal()`, this one change corrects POST, GET, list, refunds and webhook `amount`/`refunded_amount`. Error messages that include an amount are corrected too.

**Tests added:**
- `money`: formatting for CLP, JPY, KWD, EUR, BRL and USD, including negatives, zero and the int64 limits, plus a parse-then-format round trip.
- `api`: create, capture, refund, get and list for CLP, JPY, KWD and USD, checking amount, fee, refunded and remaining.
- `webhook`: payload amounts for CLP, JPY, KWD and USD.

**Things you might trip over:**
- An `Amount` with no currency set (the zero value) now renders "0" instead of "0.00". Nothing in the service renders one today.
- Merchants who received CLP/JPY/KWD webhooks before this fix got the wrong amounts in those payloads. Stored data is fine, but those consumers may need to be told.

**Not fixed, out of scope:** `money.Parse` can overflow int64 for amounts within one major unit of the maximum (e.g. "92233720368547758.99" USD), because the range check covers only the whole part before the fraction is added. It is unrelated to this ticket and I left it alone; it deserves its own ticket.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4420 is fixed: a refund is now checked against what is left on the payment, not against the original amount. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Cause:** `Service.Refund` in `payment/service.go` compared the requested amount with `p.Amount.Minor`, so any single refund up to the full amount passed regardless of earlier refunds. That is how 600.00 + 600.00 went through on a 1000.00 payment.

**Fix:** the guard now compares against `p.Remaining()` — a one-line change, with no API or constructor changes.
- A refund larger than the remaining amount returns `ErrRefundExceedsRemaining`, which the API already maps to 422 `refund_exceeds_remaining`.
- A rejected refund leaves the payment untouched: nothing is saved and no event is emitted.
- Refunding exactly the remaining amount is accepted and moves the payment to REFUNDED.

**Tests added:**
- `payment/service_test.go`: the ticket scenario (600 then 600 on 1000 is rejected, payment unchanged, then 400 completes it), plus a concurrent test that the refunded total never exceeds the amount.
- `api/api_test.go`: the same scenario over HTTP, checking the 422 code, the unchanged payment, and the final REFUNDED state with remaining "0.00".

**Behaviour I left as it was (not asked for in the ticket):**
- A refund on a payment that is already fully REFUNDED still returns 409 `invalid_transition`, not 422. If Finance or merchants expect 422 there, that is a small follow-up.
- Two refunds racing on the same payment cannot over-refund, but the loser may get 409 `conflict` rather than being retried.
- With an `Idempotency-Key`, that 409 `conflict` is stored and replayed on retry with the same key, so the merchant would need a new key. This is from reading `api/idempotency.go`, not from a test; it probably deserves its own ticket.

**Not covered here:** payments already over-refunded (like m_8812's) are not repaired by this change and still show a negative remaining amount.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary:
PAY-4432 is fixed: walking all pages now returns every payment of the merchant exactly once, in creation order, for any limit. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Cause:** `store.Memory.ListByMerchant` issued a `next_cursor` that already pointed at the first item of the next page, then added one more when reading it back. Every page after the first therefore skipped one payment. That matches the ticket: 19 follow-up pages at limit=50 lose 19 of 1,000 (981), and limit=1 loses every second one.

**Fix:** removed the extra `offset++` in `store/memory.go`. The cursor format is unchanged, so cursors issued before the fix resume at the correct position. `next_cursor` is empty on the last page, including when the total is an exact multiple of the limit. No public API or constructor changed.

**Tests added:**
- `store/memory_test.go`: `TestListWalksAllPages` walks full listings for a range of totals and limits (including 1,000 at limit 50, limit 1, exact multiples, default and capped limits, and an empty merchant) and checks order, completeness and page count. `TestListLastPageHasNoCursor` checks the last page of an exact multiple.
- `api/api_test.go`: `TestListPaymentsWalksAllPages` follows `next_cursor` over HTTP for several limits, with another merchant's payments interleaved.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
PAY-4450 is fixed: the dispatcher now follows the README retry policy. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Root cause:** `retryable` in `webhook/dispatcher.go` had the status range inverted — it retried every 4xx and treated 5xx as permanent. That one condition explains both complaints (410/400/401/404 hammered `MaxAttempts` times; 503 dead-lettered after one attempt).

**Changes**
- `webhook/dispatcher.go`: `retryable` now returns true only for transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx. Any other non-2xx status (including 3xx) goes straight to the dead-letter list after one attempt.
- `webhook/dispatcher.go`: the delivery loop now counts the sends actually made, so `DeadLetter.Attempts` is always accurate. It was already correct for normal policies; the only case that changes is `MaxAttempts <= 0`, which used to record 1 attempt without sending anything and now records 0.
- `webhook/webhook_test.go`: added tests for permanent statuses, transient statuses with the backoff schedule, exhaustion after `MaxAttempts`, a 503 followed by 410, and a cancelled context leaving the event queued.

No public API or constructor signatures changed.

**Things I left alone that you may want to decide on**
- **`LastStatus` after a transport error:** it records the status of the final attempt, so it is 0 (with `LastError` set) if that attempt was a transport error, even if an earlier attempt got a 503. I read "last HTTP status" as "status of the last attempt"; if you want "last status actually received", that's a small change.
- **Head-of-line blocking:** `Flush` delivers serially, so now that 5xx is retried, one merchant's outage delays every other merchant's events behind it for the whole backoff (up to about 31s per event with `DefaultPolicy`). Fixing that means per-merchant queues or scheduled retries, which is a separate ticket.
- **Cancellation on the final attempt:** if the context is cancelled during the last allowed send, the event is dead-lettered with the context error rather than staying queued. This predates the ticket and I did not change it.
- **Outages longer than the retry window:** with `DefaultPolicy` (6 attempts, 1s base) the retries span about 31 seconds. A real 5-minute outage like m_91's will now be retried but will still end in the dead-letter list, so the policy numbers may need revisiting on the product side.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary:
PAY-4461 is fixed: a key now expires exactly 24h after first use (now >= first use + TTL), and expired records are evicted at that point instead of lingering for two TTLs. Tests, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

There were two defects in `idempotency/store.go`:

- **Stale replay:** `Begin` never checked expiry itself and relied entirely on the purge, so an expired key kept replaying its old response (or returning key-reuse / in-progress). `Begin` now treats an expired record as absent, drops it and starts a new request whatever the fingerprint.
- **Memory growth:** the purge compared `now - ExpiresAt > ttl`, so records were only evicted 48h after first use. It now evicts as soon as a record reaches its expiry.

Semantics before expiry are unchanged, as are `NewMemory` and the `Store` interface.

I added store tests for the boundary just before and exactly at the TTL, the 40h case from the support ticket, an expired record that has not been purged yet, and eviction via `Len()`. There is also an API-level test that reuses the key after 24h and checks a new payment is created.

Things I left alone:

- **Purge trigger:** the purge still runs only from `Begin`, at most once a minute, so a store that receives no requests keeps its expired records until the next one. `Len()` still counts those, as its doc comment says.
- **`Complete` / `Release`:** these do not check expiry. A request that runs longer than the TTL could complete onto a record that a newer request with the same key has since created. This was already possible and needs a per-request token to fix properly, so it is out of scope here.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary:
PAY-4475 is fixed: domain errors return their documented status and code again, however much context they are wrapped in. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean.

**Root cause:** `api/errors.go` compared errors with `switch err { case payment.ErrNotFound: ... }`. Once last week's release wrapped errors with `%w`, nothing matched and everything fell through to 500.

**Fix (`api/errors.go`):** `errorResponse` now matches with `errors.Is` against an ordered table of the sentinel errors. Status codes, error codes and messages are as in the README; anything unrecognised is still 500 `internal_error` with the generic "internal error" message.

**One change outside the API layer, for you to confirm (`payment/service.go`):** `Create` now wraps a `money.Fee` failure with `%v` instead of `%w`. That failure can only come from a bad `FeeBps` configuration, and it carries `money.ErrInvalidAmount`. With `errors.Is` matching it would have turned into a 400 `invalid_request` blaming the client and hiding a server misconfiguration from the 5xx alert. The cost is that this one line departs from the README's "always wrap with `%w`" convention (commented in place), and callers can no longer match `money.ErrInvalidAmount` on that path. If you would rather keep the convention, revert the line and drop the "fee misconfiguration" test case.

**Tests added (`api/api_test.go`):**
- End-to-end cases for 404, 409, 422 and 400 across get, authorize, capture, decline, refund, create and list, including requests sent with an `Idempotency-Key`.
- A unit test that every mapped sentinel is recognised bare, deeply wrapped and inside `errors.Join`.
- A test that a repository failure and a fee misconfiguration both stay 500 with the generic message.

`ErrDuplicate` is not in the README's list, so it stays unmapped and returns 500.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary:
PAY-4488 is fixed: `Policy.Backoff` no longer overflows, so the enterprise policy (48 attempts, 1s base, 1h cap) now waits 1s, 2s, … 2048s and then 1h for every remaining attempt. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Cause:** `Backoff` computed `BaseDelay << (n-1)`. With a 1s base the shift overflows `time.Duration` at attempt 35 and goes negative, then becomes 0 from attempt 65. A negative value slips past the `d > MaxDelay` check, so the dispatcher slept for a negative duration, i.e. not at all.

**Fix (`webhook/dispatcher.go`):** the delay is now doubled step by step and checked against `MaxDelay` before each doubling, so it cannot overflow. For any attempt number and any positive `BaseDelay`/`MaxDelay` the result is positive, never decreases and is capped at `MaxDelay`. The schedule for attempts that did not overflow before is unchanged, and no signatures changed.

**Behaviour changes at the edges:**
- An attempt number below 1 is treated as 1; previously it panicked on a negative shift count.
- A policy with a non-positive `BaseDelay` or `MaxDelay` returns 0 (no backoff). This matches the old result for zero values; a negative setting used to yield a negative wait and now yields 0 — both mean no sleep.

**Tests (`webhook/webhook_test.go`):** added three tests:
- positive / non-decreasing / capped checks across several policies up to attempt 200 and `math.MaxInt`;
- edge cases, including the attempts where the shift used to go negative and reach zero;
- a dispatcher-level test that runs the enterprise policy against a permanently failing endpoint and asserts all 47 sleeps.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
PAY-4502 is implemented: merchants can cancel a payment before capture. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

- **Status:** added `payment.StatusCanceled` ("CANCELED"). It is final, and `ParseStatus` accepts it case-insensitively.
- **Service:** added `Service.Cancel(ctx, id)`. It is allowed from CREATED and PENDING only; anything else wraps `ErrInvalidTransition`, and unknown ids wrap `ErrNotFound`. A successful cancel emits `payment.canceled`.
- **HTTP:** added `POST /payments/{id}/cancel`, returning 200 with the payment body, 409 `invalid_transition` when not cancelable, and 404 `not_found` for unknown ids. Any request body is ignored, as with authorize and capture.
- **Canceled payments are closed:** authorize, capture, decline, refund and a second cancel all return 409. The existing transition guards already reject unknown states, so those methods are unchanged.
- **Webhook:** no dispatcher change was needed, since it forwards any event type. I did not add a webhook-level test for `payment.canceled`; the event is asserted at the service level only.
- **Tests and docs:** added service and API tests covering the acceptance criteria, and updated the README lifecycle diagram and event list.

A cancel that races with a capture loses on the optimistic version check and returns 409 `conflict` rather than `invalid_transition`, as with the other transitions.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
PAY-4510: `GET /merchants/{merchantID}/payments` now accepts an optional, case-insensitive `status` and paginates over the filtered result. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Needs follow-up before release:** the production database-backed `payment.Repository` is not in this repo. It must honour the new `Page.Status` field; until it does, it will silently return unfiltered results. The requirement is documented on the interface.

What changed:
- **Filter plumbing:** `payment.Page` gained a `Status` field (empty means no filter). The `Repository` interface, `Service.List` signature and all constructors are unchanged, so existing fakes and other teams' tests still compile.
- **Handler (`api/handlers.go`):** parses `status` with the existing `payment.ParseStatus`; an unknown value returns 400 `invalid_request`.
- **Service (`payment/service.go`):** `List` also validates and normalises `Page.Status`, so non-HTTP callers get the same error instead of an empty list.
- **Store (`store/memory.go`):** `ListByMerchant` filters while scanning, fills each page to `limit` matches, and only issues a `next_cursor` if a further match exists. Without `status` the output and cursors are identical to before.
- **Tests and docs:** new store, service and API tests cover sparse matches, a non-matching tail, no matches, unknown status and the unfiltered path; README has a short "Listing" section.

Behaviours you might not assume:
- An empty `status=` is treated as absent, matching how `limit` is handled, rather than rejected.
- Surrounding whitespace in `status` is accepted, because `ParseStatus` trims it.
- If a payment changes status while a client is walking pages, it can be missed or show up under its new status; ordering is unaffected and nothing is returned twice.
- A filtered listing with few matches scans the merchant's whole payment list under the read lock. That is fine in memory; the database implementation will want an index on merchant and status.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary:
PAY-4523 is implemented: `Dispatcher.Replay` and `POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay` behave as the acceptance criteria describe. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**What changed**
- `webhook/dispatcher.go`: new exported `ErrDeadLetterNotFound` and `Replay(ctx, eventID) (delivered bool, err error)`. The private `deliver` is split so Replay can see the outcome of the retry loop; `Flush` behaviour is unchanged.
- `api`: new route and handler returning `200 {"event_id": ..., "delivered": ...}`; `ErrDeadLetterNotFound` maps to `404 not_found`.
- README webhook section documents the endpoint.
- New tests in `webhook/webhook_test.go` and `api/api_test.go`; existing tests are untouched.

**Behaviour the ticket did not specify — please confirm**
- **Cancelled mid-replay:** if the context is done during the backoff (e.g. ops closes the HTTP connection), Replay returns the context error and puts the original dead letter back unchanged. Otherwise the event would be lost from the list. Over HTTP this surfaces as `500 internal_error`.
- **Merchant no longer has an endpoint:** Replay returns `(false, nil)` and the event stays dead-lettered with 0 attempts and a `LastError` explaining why. A fresh event in this situation is silently dropped by `Flush`; I did not want a replay to report success or lose the event.
- **Concurrent replays of the same event:** only one delivers; the others get `ErrDeadLetterNotFound` (404).

**Worth knowing**
- The endpoint is synchronous, so the request blocks for the full retry policy. With the production policy that is about 31s of backoff plus up to 6 sends at the 10s client timeout. Callers behind a short proxy timeout would trigger the cancellation path above.
- The replay endpoint does not take an `Idempotency-Key`; the ticket did not ask for it.
- A panicking `Sender` during a replay would lose the event from the list; `Flush` has the same pre-existing gap and I left both alone.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
PAY-4530 is implemented: both POST endpoints accept `amount_minor`, payment responses carry the new integer fields, and cross-format retries replay. Tests with `-race`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**What changed**
- `api/dto.go`: `createPaymentRequest` and `refundRequest` gain `amount_minor`. Payment responses add `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor`, `remaining_minor`, and each refund adds `amount_minor`. All existing fields are untouched, and since every endpoint goes through `toPaymentResponse`, the list endpoint is covered too.
- `api/handlers.go`: a new `requestAmount` helper, used by create and refund, resolves the amount from either field. Neither present returns 400 `invalid_request`; both present must denote the same value in the request's currency (the payment's currency for refunds), otherwise 400.
- Idempotency needed no code change: the fingerprint was already computed from the decoded minor units and currency, so `"amount":"10.50"` and `"amount_minor":1050` hash the same. I added tests to pin this for create and refund.
- Unknown fields are still rejected; the decoder is unchanged.
- `api/api_test.go` has new tests for the above (existing tests untouched), and `README.md` documents the new field and the cross-format replay.

**Behaviours worth knowing**
- `amount_minor` must be a literal JSON integer: `"1050"`, `10.5`, `1050.0` and values beyond int64 all return 400.
- An explicit `null` counts as absent, so `{"amount":"10.50","amount_minor":null}` is a valid legacy request.
- When both fields are sent, the legacy `amount` is still fully validated; `"amount":""` alongside a valid `amount_minor` is a 400.
- On refunds the payment is still looked up first, as before, so an unknown payment returns 404 even if the amount fields are also invalid.
- Idempotent responses stored before this deploy replay without the new `*_minor` fields until their 24h expiry.

**Not changed**
- Webhook payloads still carry only decimal strings; the ticket covers API endpoints only. Say if you want `*_minor` there too.
- `money.Parse` has an existing overflow at the very top of the int64 range (e.g. `"92233720368547758.99"` USD wraps negative). It still ends in a 400 because the amount is then non-positive, so I left it; it deserves its own ticket.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary:
PAY-4541 is done: `payment.CanTransition(from, to Status) bool` now holds the allowed status changes, and every service method validates through it. `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race ./...` all pass.

- **`payment/payment.go`**: added `CanTransition` with exactly the five transitions from the ticket. Everything else is false, including self transitions and unknown statuses.
- **`payment/service.go`**: the four `switch p.Status` blocks are gone. `Authorize`, `Capture` and `Decline` go through a small unexported helper that checks `CanTransition` and sets the status. `Refund` checks `CanTransition(p.Status, StatusRefunded)` up front for both partial and full refunds, so a partial refund is allowed exactly when a full one would be.
- **Behaviour**: unchanged. Error messages are identical ("cannot authorize a X payment", still wrapping `ErrInvalidTransition`), the order of checks in `Refund` is the same (status, then currency, then remaining), and events and returned payments are as before. `NewService` and the other public signatures are untouched.
- **Tests added in `payment/service_test.go`**:
  - an exhaustive `CanTransition` matrix, including unknown and empty statuses;
  - rejected operations on a REFUNDED payment keep their messages, leave the payment unchanged and publish nothing;
  - `Refund` reports a wrong status before a currency or amount problem.
- **`README.md`**: one sentence in the lifecycle section pointing at `CanTransition`.

One thing left alone: `Status.Final()` in `payment.go` still hard-codes DECLINED and REFUNDED as final, so it is a second place that knows something about transitions. I did not derive it from `CanTransition` because it is public API outside the ticket's scope, and a naive derivation would change its result for unknown statuses from false to true. It is worth a follow-up ticket.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
PAY-4555 is fixed: `idempotency.Memory` is now safe for concurrent use, and for a given key only one concurrent `Begin` can start the request. `go test -race -count=3 ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are all clean.

**Root cause (both in `idempotency/store.go`)**
- **Crash / DATA RACE:** `Complete` and `Release` read the records map (and `Complete` wrote the record) without holding the mutex.
- **Duplicate refunds:** `Begin` looked the key up, dropped the lock, then re-took it to insert. Two simultaneous retries could both miss the record and both get `started=true`.

**Fix**
- `Begin` now does purge, lookup and reservation in a single critical section.
- `Complete` and `Release` hold the mutex for their whole body.
- No change to the public API, the constructor, the errors or the expiry behaviour.

**Tests added**
- `idempotency/store_test.go`: 64 concurrent `Begin` calls on one key must yield exactly one start and `ErrInProgress` for the rest, then all replay after `Complete`. A second test hammers `Begin`/`Complete`/`Release`/`Len` on shared keys while the clock advances, for the race detector.
- `api/api_test.go`: 32 concurrent refund retries with the same `Idempotency-Key` must produce exactly one refund; the others get a replay or `409 request_in_progress`.

**Not changed, worth knowing**
`Complete` and `Release` still act on whatever record currently holds the key. If a request runs longer than the 24h TTL and the key is re-begun in the meantime, the late `Complete` would write onto the new record. This is not the bug in the ticket and fixing it would mean changing the `Store` interface, so I left it; say if you want a follow-up ticket.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
PAY-4561 is fixed: `store.Memory` now deep-copies every payment on the way in and on the way out, so concurrent refunds no longer race and a version-conflicted update leaves nothing behind. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Root cause:** `store.Memory` stored and returned `payment.Payment` by plain struct copy, but `Payment.Refunds` is a slice, so every copy shared one backing array with the stored payment. Two concurrent `Service.Refund` calls both appended into that array's spare capacity. The call that lost the version check could still overwrite the slot the winner had just persisted — the phantom refund id and the mismatch with `refunded_amount`.

**Fix (`store/memory.go` only):** `Create`, `Get`, `Update` and `ListByMerchant` now use the existing `Payment.Clone()`. The version check, increment and error wrapping are untouched, so optimistic-locking semantics are unchanged. No public API or constructor changed.

**Tests added (`store/memory_test.go`):**
- `TestStoredPaymentIsIsolatedFromCallers` checks that none of the four methods share the `Refunds` slice with callers.
- `TestVersionConflictLeavesNoTrace` is a deterministic winner/loser case: after the conflict the stored payment holds only the winner's refund.
- `TestConcurrentRefundsAreConsistent` runs 8 goroutines refunding one payment through `payment.Service`. It checks that every stored refund was returned to a caller, that amounts add up to `Refunded`, and that the version matches the number of successes.

With the clones in `Get` and `Update` temporarily removed, the isolation and concurrent tests failed with the ticket's symptoms (refund ids never returned to a caller, sum not matching `Refunded`); I then restored the fix. That run was stopped by those assertion failures and printed no DATA RACE report, so the race itself is confirmed fixed only by the clean `-race` runs.

**Not changed:** `Service.mutate` hands the same `Refunds` slice to both the published event and the returned payment. Nothing mutates it today (the webhook dispatcher serialises the event synchronously inside `Publish`), so I left it as outside the ticket; an `ev.Payment = p.Clone()` there would be a one-line hardening if you want it.

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
PAY-4570: `Begin` no longer scans the store, so its cost is independent of how many keys are held.

**Cause:** every `Begin` called `purgeLocked`, which copied all records into a slice and sorted them by expiry while holding the store mutex. That is O(n log n) per request, and with a 24h TTL the store keeps growing until a restart.

**Fix (`idempotency/store.go`):** records now sit in a creation-ordered `container/list` alongside the lookup map. Every record gets the same TTL, so creation order is expiry order and the purge only pops expired records off the front, stopping at the first live one. `Release` unlinks the record directly, so released keys leave nothing behind.

**Expiry semantics are unchanged:**
- A key is expired once now >= ExpiresAt, and `Begin` still checks expiry on lookup, so an expired key is never replayed.
- Expired records are still evicted on every `Begin`; I did not need the once-per-minute allowance.
- `NewMemory`, the `Store` interface, `Record` and `Len` are untouched.

**Behaviour to be aware of:** the first `Begin` after a quiet period evicts everything that expired in the meantime, so that single call costs time proportional to the number of records it evicts. It does not depend on the number of live keys.

**Verification:** `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are all clean. I added tests in `idempotency/store_test.go` for the exact expiry boundary, eviction of expired records while live ones are kept, release followed by a retry, and a regression guard that runs 2,000 `Begin` calls against 50,000 live keys under a loose 2s bound. There is also a `BenchmarkBeginLargeStore`, which I could not run here because the tool does not allow `-bench`, so I have no measured per-call figure.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4588: `money.Allocate` now honours its documented contract, so split payouts always sum exactly to the charge. `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race ./...` are clean.

**Cause:** each part was computed in `float64` and rounded independently with `math.Round`, so the parts could sum to less than the charge (33.33 × 3 = 99.99) or more (0.05 split 1:1 → 0.03 + 0.03). It also broke the package rule that money never touches floating point, and lost precision above 2^53 minor units.

**Fix (`money/allocate.go`):** exact integer largest-remainder allocation.
- Each part starts at the floor of its exact share.
- The leftover minor units go one each to the parts with the largest fractional remainder, ties broken by lower index.
- A part whose share is exact, including any zero-ratio part, never receives an extra unit.

The ticket's three cases now give 33.34 + 33.33 + 33.33, 0.02 × 3 + 0.01 × 4 = 0.10, and 0.03 + 0.02.

The arithmetic uses `math/big` (stdlib), because neither the sum of the ratios nor amount × ratio is guaranteed to fit in an `int64`. This means no valid input fails on overflow, at the cost of a few small allocations per part.

Signature, validation and error values (`ErrInvalidAmount`) are unchanged. `Allocate` has no callers elsewhere in the repo, so nothing else needed touching.

**Tests (`money/money_test.go`):** added `TestAllocateReconciles`, a table covering the ticket's cases, tie-breaking, zero ratios, zero amount, JPY and KWD exponents, amounts beyond float64 precision, and `MaxInt64` amount with `MaxInt64` ratios. `TestAllocateErrors` gained the empty-ratios and negative-ratio cases. Existing tests are untouched.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
Retries with the same `Idempotency-Key` now replay the original response when the request is the same after parsing, for both `POST /payments` and `POST /payments/{id}/refunds`. Tests (with `-race`), `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Cause:** the fingerprint was a hash of the raw request body, so the SDK's rebuilt JSON (key order, whitespace, `"usd"`, `"10.5"`) looked like a different request and got `422 idempotency_key_reused`.

**Fix:** the fingerprint is now built from the parsed values:
- **Create:** merchant id, amount in minor units, and normalised currency code.
- **Refund:** payment id, amount in minor units, and the payment's currency.

A genuinely different request on the same key (other amount, currency or merchant) is still rejected with 422. Merchant id is compared exactly, so `m_310` and `M_310` are different requests.

**Changes:**
- `api/idempotency.go`: replaced `bodyFingerprint` with `createFingerprint` and `refundFingerprint`.
- `api/handlers.go`: both handlers compute the fingerprint after parsing.
- `api/api_test.go`: added tests using the ticket's two captured examples, checking that only one payment or refund exists afterwards and that different requests still get 422.
- `README.md`: the Idempotency section now says what "the same request" means.

No public API, constructor or `idempotency.Store` change.

**Things I left alone that you may want to follow up on:**
- **Duplicate payments:** I found no path where one key creates two payments. The duplicates in the ticket fit the first POST succeeding server-side, the retry getting 422, and the customer retrying under a new key. That should stop with this fix, but I did not confirm it against production data.
- **Retry while the first request is still running:** this still returns `409 request_in_progress`, as documented. The SDK needs to back off and retry on that code.
- **Transient 409 `conflict` is stored and replayed:** a refund that loses an optimistic-lock race will keep returning that 409 for the same key. Only 5xx responses are released for retry today.
- **Keys are not scoped per merchant:** two merchants using the same key on `POST /payments` collide and the second gets 422. There is no authentication context in this service to scope by.
- **Persistent idempotency stores:** if any environment uses one, keys recorded before this deploy hold old-format fingerprints and their retries will get 422 until they expire (24h). The in-memory store in `cmd/server` is unaffected.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary:
PAY-4601 is fixed: `money.Fee` now computes the fee in exact integer arithmetic and rounds half-to-even, as its doc comment promises. The full suite passes with `-race`; `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

**Cause:** `Fee` used `math.Ceil` on a `float64` product. That always rounded up (10.05 USD at 290 bps is 29.145, charged as 30 instead of 29) and lost precision above 2^53 minor units, which explains the large-amount drift.

**Fix (`money/fee.go`):** the amount is split into whole and fractional multiples of 10000 before multiplying, so nothing overflows for any amount up to `math.MaxInt64` with bps in [0, 10000]. Signature, validation and error behaviour are unchanged.

**Tests (`money/money_test.go`):** added the ticket example, tie cases in both directions, a `math/big` comparison on amounts around 2^53 and up to `MaxInt64`, an exhaustive small-amount sweep, and a negative-bps rejection case.

**Not changed, needs follow-up:**
- **Historical fees:** this only corrects fees on new payments. Fees already stored on existing payments were computed with the old rounding; any correction or re-statement is a separate decision for finance.
- **`money.Allocate` overflow:** it computes `a.Minor * r` in `int64`, which can overflow for very large amounts or ratios and break its sum-exactly contract. It is outside this ticket, so I left it alone; it deserves its own ticket.
